01_completion_curves.png: Cumulative incidence, not a completed-only CDF. AE128 finishes only 4/500 predictions; Agent 493/493; AE32 476/500. The vertical line is 170 ms from action start.
02_outcomes_and_latency_quantiles.png: Top: on-time, late and missing outcomes over every decision. Bottom: conditional P50/P99; four AE128 observations cannot characterize typical session latency or a reliable tail.
03_payload_statistics_and_time.png: Plot 03 now contains only P50/P99 payload bars on one shared linear scale. Median application payload: Agent 117.3 kB, AE128/8-bit 2,339.1 kB, AE32/8-bit 600.2 kB. The original filename is kept to preserve links; timelines have moved to 13_payload_time_and_relative_variation.png. Data and statistics are unchanged.
04_snr_mcs_time.png: Per-transmission PUSCH measurements, not MAC-log SNR. One-second medians and the full within-bin SNR range make dense radio records legible; start-up/high-SNR values are retained when inside the transmitted-frame window. P50/P99 use all raw events. The same FAVORABLE_STABLE trace is used, but wall-clock and scene timing differ across sessions. Commanded targets remain in CHANNEL_COMMANDS.csv.
05_prediction_feedback_time.png: Raw per-decision prediction and feedback latencies. The AE128 overload appears as missing milestones across most of the session, not artificially low latency. No causal downlink or packet-loss attribution is made.
06_deadline_quality.png: All values come unchanged from the sealed campaign report. Recall uses 1.0 m vehicle / 1.2 m pedestrian tolerance; precision uses the existing 3 m matching gate and only timely predictions. It can be high even when very few predictions are timely. AE32 recall/IoU are upper bounds; AE128 precision is undefined, not zero. The boundary here is prediction readiness, not UE-feedback receipt.
07_scene_complexity_and_q_time.png: Agent only: camera SI, radar P40, dropping control q, application payload and measured PUSCH SNR in five aligned panels. SI/P40 are reconstructed from the recorded 22-D state using the pinned scaling constants. Each payload is the SFD4 application-frame size for the same policy decision, in decimal kB. Holds and fallbacks are excluded from the first four panels, whose values are unsmoothed. The fifth panel uses all retained per-transmission PUSCH SNR events in the session, shown as one-second medians with a minimum–maximum band, including startup extremes. Empty bins stay absent. Radio is aligned by telemetry-ingest wall time, not by frame; measured PUSCH SNR is not the commanded SNR given to the actor or the MAC-log power-control statistic. Alignment shows association, not causal feature attribution. Static configurations remain excluded.
08_map_freshness_cdf_and_time.png: The successful-install CDF alone hides AE128's overload: only four updates occur. The time-weighted AoI CDF and timeline expose the ensuing approximately 123-second no-update period. Before the first install AoI is undefined; no-map duration is listed in METRICS.json. Frame-level age is not object-track age or policy-feedback latency.
09_perception_time.png: Optional detail figure: per-frame localisation recall and Q_perc on scored, defined samples. Empty intervals are not zero quality. Do not average these displayed recalls to recover pooled object recall; denominators differ by frame. The campaign-level deadline-aware comparison is plot 06.
10_map_freshness_quantiles.png: Conditional successful-install latency versus time-weighted latest-installed-frame age. AE128 successful-install P50 is 470 ms, but its session AoI P50 is 61.7 seconds because updates stop. Log scale on the AoI panel, linear milliseconds on install latency. Numbers and initial no-map durations are in METRICS.json.
13_payload_time_and_relative_variation.p: Absolute payload time series only, on one shared linear kB scale with no smoothing. All 1,000 sent frames per configuration, including holds and fallbacks, remain included. Equal elapsed time is not a paired scene. The relative-variation panel has been removed; the original filename is retained to preserve links.
